sentence_stem: Although she has a lot of homework,
correct_completion: she still wants to go to the cinema.
full_sentence: Although she has a lot of homework, she still wants to go to the cinema.
acceptable_variants: she still plans to go out with friends.
she still wants to go to the party.

options.text: so she has to stay at home.
options.why_wrong: 'So' shows a result, not a contrast. 'Although' needs a clause that contrasts with the first part.

options.text: she has to finish it by Monday.
options.why_wrong: This repeats the homework idea instead of showing a contrast with 'although'.

options.text: she still wants to go to the cinema.
she has a big test tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This adds a reason to study, but it does not create a contrast with the first part of the sentence.

explanation: After 'although', the second clause must show contrast with the first clause. Learners often choose a clause with a result or reason connector because those connectors are used more often in their first language habits.
translation: Aunque tiene mucha tarea, todavía quiere ir al cine.
